rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest borderline: chunk 4 "Linear: first-party MCP (official)" line 77: "Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path." "The three trackers" resolves against GitHub Issues (chunk 2), Jira (chunk 3), and Linear (chunk 4, current) — all three named and elaborated by this point in the sequential read. Stays inside; no never-named, vague, or re-chunk-stranded referent found anywhere else in the file.

No callback to another curriculum file by position anywhere in the body (this is a standalone reference lookup page with no lecture/exercise cross-references). Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 15: "Plugins distribute Path 2, `claude mcp add`, at scale, under *Plugins and marketplaces*." — names the target section by title, satisfying the carve-out ("name it, don't locate it").

Closest/shortest chunk: chunk 5 "Other trackers" lines 83-88: "Check the [Anthropic Directory] for reviewed connectors and your tracker's own docs. Most have a third-party MCP or a CLI fallback (like `gh`)." One paragraph, but a self-carrying claim (the fallback path for any tracker not individually covered) — not a wait-state or context-dependent bullet. All other chunks carry substantially more content.

Closest borderline: chunk 5 header "Other trackers (Asana, Shortcut, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, etc.)" (line 83) against body (lines 85-87) that never names those four apps individually. Header is a category label naming illustrative examples; body delivers generic guidance for the class of "other trackers," which is what the header promises — it doesn't contradict, it just doesn't itemize per-app, which the header never claimed either. All 8 headers checked; all match their chunk's content.

Checked every sub-item across all 8 chunks. "Not X. Not Y. Z.": none (closest surface form is line 13's clipped "No MCP." inside a list item — a single fragment, not the triple-negation pattern). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none found. Self-grading superlative: line 77 "Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers" grades an external product (Linear), not the training's own value, so it does not trip the value-prop-leak clause. Number + own retraction: none — every date (e.g. line 46 "GA on 2026-02-04") is a plain unhedged fact. Abstraction-noun stacks: none — language stays concrete (endpoint, PAT, OAuth, marketplace.json). Empty-leg verb triplets: none.
